To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the pancreatic fluid secretion depends on the presence of sodium ions in the bathing medium, that sodium ions enter the secreted fluid via a paracellular pathway and that the sodium ions are essential for the fluid secretion.
Na+ is the only monovalent cation that is secreted in the pancreatic fluid and that this secretion is due to the active Na+ transport across the basolateral membrane of the pancreatic duct cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of Na+ in the fluid transport of pancreatic ductular cells, and with the mechanisms by which Na+ and other electrolytes move across these cells.
the mechanism of electrolyte transport in the pancreas and the role of sodium ions.
the role of sodium ions (Na+) in the secretion of pancreatic fluid in the rabbit.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the pancreatic secretion of electrolyte-rich fluid is a function of a Na+‐dependent active transport of Cl‐ across the acinar cells and a Na+‐ and Cl‐‐dependent passive paracellular flow of electrolyte and water.
pancreatic fluid secretion is an active process, in which Na+ is actively transported from the blood side to the luminal side.
the role of sodium ions (Na+) in pancreatic fluid secretion is that they are the driving force for fluid secretion.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the secreted fluid of the rabbit pancreas is a NaCl‐solution with an increased K+ concentration, which is secreted through the ductular epithelium and the acinar cells by active Na+ transport.
the pancreatic ductular epithelium is an electrically tight epithelium with a paracellular pathway for electrolyte movements.
the secreted pancreatic fluid is a solution of the composition of the interstitial fluid, and that NaCl and KCl are the major electrolytes involved in the fluid secretion.
The main takeaway from our work is that
sodium ions are important for pancreatic secretion.
the pancreas is a great model system for studying ion and fluid transport in general.
sodium ions play a crucial role in pancreatic fluid secretion.
